quests.hint: Pause briefly after 'Friday', then say the rest in one go.
quests.explanation: The 'if' clause is one thought group and the invitation is another. A short pause at the boundary helps the listener follow.
quests.textToSpeak: If you're free on Friday, we could grab lunch.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's phrasing as you repeat.

quests.hint: Pause after 'open'; keep 'head straight to the main hall' together.
quests.explanation: A clause that sets the time is usually separated from the instruction that follows. The pause after 'open' lets the listener prepare.
quests.textToSpeak: When the doors open, please head straight to the main hall.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Pause after 'in'; then let the second half flow.
quests.explanation: The pause marks where the condition ends and the result begins. Keep 'the dashboard should load automatically' together.
quests.textToSpeak: Once you've logged in, the dashboard should load automatically.
quests.instruction: Copy the phrasing and breath groups as closely as you can.

quests.hint: Say 'the report on customer feedback' as one chunk, then pause.
quests.explanation: A noun phrase and its modifier belong together, so 'the report on customer feedback' is one group. Pausing after it, not inside it, makes the sentence easy to follow.
quests.textToSpeak: The report on customer feedback is due next week.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Keep 'the train to Manchester' together, then pause briefly.
quests.explanation: The subject and its 'to' phrase form one group. Splitting them ('the train / to Manchester') would confuse the listener.
quests.textToSpeak: The train to Manchester leaves from platform nine.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Chunk 'the woman at the front desk' before you continue.
quests.explanation: A long subject is easier to follow when spoken as one unit. A short pause then lets 'gave' begin the next group.
quests.textToSpeak: The woman at the front desk gave us a map.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and pause where they pause.

quests.hint: Pause after 'Monday' and after 'May'.
quests.explanation: Dates split naturally into pieces, and the pauses show which piece is which. This also prevents listeners from missing details.
quests.textToSpeak: On Monday, the fourteenth of May, we're closed.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Short pauses after 'nine' and 'five'.
quests.explanation: The three actions have the same grammar, so speaking each one as its own group keeps the pattern easy to follow. Without the pauses, a list of times can blur into one long string.
quests.textToSpeak: We open at nine, close at five, and stay shut on Sundays.
quests.instruction: Listen for the pauses, then repeat with the same chunks.

quests.hint: Pause after 'adults'; keep 'five for children' together.
quests.explanation: The comma marks a contrast, so each side gets its own group. The second 'are' is left out, so a slight pause shows it.
quests.textToSpeak: Tickets are ten pounds for adults, five for children.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's phrasing as you repeat.

quests.hint: Chunk 'the person who called earlier' before the verb.
quests.explanation: The relative clause is part of the subject, so pausing before 'who' or inside it would split a single idea. The natural break comes before the verb 'left'.
quests.textToSpeak: The person who called earlier left a message.
quests.instruction: Listen for the pauses, then repeat with the same chunks.

quests.hint: Keep 'the manager we spoke to yesterday' as one phrase.
quests.explanation: A pause after 'spoke to' would leave the listener waiting for a verb that has not arrived. Keeping the whole subject together makes it clear who 'is on leave'.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager we spoke to yesterday is on leave.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Pause after 'yet'.
quests.explanation: The subject is long, so the listener needs a short pause to hold it in mind before hearing the instruction. The pause falls at the end of the subject, not inside it.
quests.textToSpeak: Anyone who hasn't signed in yet should do that now.
quests.instruction: Copy the phrasing and breath groups as closely as you can.

quests.hint: Say 'by the way' quickly and quietly between two pauses.
quests.explanation: An aside is spoken faster and at a lower pitch, so the main message stays clear. The commas show where the aside begins and ends.
quests.textToSpeak: Our new office, by the way, opens in June.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Lower and speed up 'as you might expect'.
quests.explanation: The parenthetical phrase interrupts the main sentence, so it is quicker and lower in pitch than the words around it.
quests.textToSpeak: The results, as you might expect, were mixed.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Pause before 'or at least'.
quests.explanation: An afterthought that softens a promise sounds honest when it is separated from the promise. Without the pause, 'or at least I hope so' can sound like part of the deadline.
quests.textToSpeak: We'll finish by five, or at least I hope so.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and pause where they pause.

quests.hint: Group the digits as 4, 3, 3 with a small pause between.
quests.explanation: Phone numbers are chunked so the listener can write them down. Keep the pitch level within each group and fall at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: My number is oh-seven-seven-oh, nine-one-four, three-two-two.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Say the code in short groups.
quests.explanation: A code is a string of unrelated pieces, so the listener cannot guess what comes next. Short groups with tiny pauses give them time to write each part down.
quests.textToSpeak: The code is A-F-seven, four-two, Q.
quests.instruction: Listen for the pauses, then repeat with the same chunks.

quests.hint: Pause after each part of the address.
quests.explanation: An address splits into number and street, apartment, and city. Pausing at each boundary helps the listener write it down.
quests.textToSpeak: It's fifty-eight Mill Street, apartment three, Denver.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's phrasing as you repeat.

quests.hint: Say 'in the middle of the night' without stopping.
quests.explanation: A prepositional phrase like 'in the middle of the night' should be spoken as one unit. Pausing inside it would sound choppy.
quests.textToSpeak: We were up in the middle of the night.
quests.instruction: Listen for the pauses, then repeat with the same chunks.

quests.hint: Do not pause inside 'the corner of Fifth and Main'.
quests.explanation: A location is understood as one place, so breaking it up ('the corner / of Fifth') makes listeners wonder if there are two locations. Speaking it as one unit keeps the direction clear.
quests.textToSpeak: It's on the corner of Fifth and Main.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Avoid pausing before 'the end of the meeting'.
quests.explanation: Breaking 'the end of the meeting' into pieces makes speech sound choppy. Say it as one chunk with stress on END and MEET-ing.
quests.textToSpeak: They arrived at the end of the meeting.
quests.instruction: Copy the phrasing and breath groups as closely as you can.

quests.hint: Pause at each semicolon.
quests.explanation: Steps are chunked one by one, and each chunk begins with a new action. The pauses help someone follow the instructions.
quests.textToSpeak: First, open the settings; then choose your language; finally, restart the app.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Group into three directions.
quests.explanation: Directions are followed one step at a time, so each step needs its own group. A short pause after 'lights' and 'blocks' lets the listener picture each step before the next arrives.
quests.textToSpeak: Turn left at the lights, go straight for two blocks, and it's on your right.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Pause after 'eggs' and 'gently'.
quests.explanation: Instructions form short, separate groups: ADD, STIR, LET REST. A pause after each helps the listener follow.
quests.textToSpeak: Add the eggs, stir gently, and let the mixture rest for ten minutes.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and pause where they pause.

quests.hint: Pause slightly before 'surprisingly good'.
quests.explanation: A short pause before the surprising part makes listeners expect something, and 'well' buys the speaker thinking time. The result sounds more natural than delivering the whole sentence at one steady pace.
quests.textToSpeak: The results were, well, surprisingly good.
quests.instruction: Repeat, keeping each thought group together.

quests.hint: Pause after 'is'.
quests.explanation: The pause creates suspense before the reveal. It works because the listener is waiting for a name, so the silence has a purpose.
quests.textToSpeak: And the winner is... Amelia Tran.
quests.instruction: Listen for the pauses, then repeat with the same chunks.

quests.hint: Say each sentence separately with a fall.
quests.explanation: Three short sentences, each with a fall, build tension. Separate them with clear pauses.
quests.textToSpeak: We tried everything. Nothing worked. Until Tuesday.
quests.instruction: Follow the speaker's phrasing as you repeat.

quests.hint: Pause after 'coming' and after 'overview'.
quests.explanation: An opening that lays out a plan is easier to follow when each stage is its own group. The listener hears 'greeting, then plan, then next step' instead of one long stream.
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks for coming. I'll start with a quick overview, then take questions.
quests.instruction: Listen for the pauses, then repeat with the same chunks.

quests.hint: Pause after 'tight'.
quests.explanation: The two problems are separate ideas joined by 'and', so each deserves its own pitch fall. Listeners then treat them as two issues, not one.
quests.textToSpeak: The main issue is that the schedule is too tight, and the budget hasn't changed.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the same chunks and pauses.

quests.hint: Pause after 'March'; peak on TEST.
quests.explanation: The condition and the result are different thoughts, so the pause after 'March' shows where the first ends. Putting the peak on TEST tells the audience what the delay buys them.
quests.textToSpeak: If we move the launch to March, we'll have time to test.
quests.instruction: Copy the phrasing and breath groups as closely as you can.
